title: @for tracks a stable identity, never the index, for reorderable or filtered lists
statement: `@for` loops over data that can reorder, filter, or have items inserted/removed track a stable field on the item (an id), not `$index` and not the whole object reference when the object is recreated on every emission.
rationale: `track $index` (or an unstable object identity) makes Angular reuse the DOM node for a position instead of for an item: as soon as the list reorders or filters, form inputs, focus, `signal()`-backed local component state and animations attach to the wrong row. `track run.id` is correct because a run keeps its id across every re-render regardless of position.

bad.caption: Tracking by index on a filtered list: rows silently swap identity when the filter changes.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, split out from QS-NG-007 because index-tracking is a correctness bug rather than a style preference.
